analysis.title: DB Research, Europe
key_insights: Deutsche Bank downgraded Hugo Boss (BOSSn.DE) to Sell from Hold and cut its target to EUR30.5 from EUR42 (last close EUR38.49). Sales are falling and the distribution network is still being reset. Management said wholesale order intake for the upcoming season is still below the prior year.

DB cut Hugo Boss EBIT forecasts by about 3% for FY26, 23% for FY27 and 19% for FY28. It is about 16% below consensus EBIT for FY27 and about 23% below for FY28, and sees no near-term recovery because operating leverage is missing.

DB cut SOBI (SOBIV.ST) to Hold from Buy with the target unchanged at SEK515 (last close SEK496.6). The stock hit new highs after a Q3 beat and raise, and the CEO departs at year end with no successor named. DB calls the IONS Q3 update a material negative for the Tryngolza sHTG launch: the FY26 guide was cut to $50m from $100m and Q3 revenue was $9m.

DB raised its Bayer (BAYGn.DE) target to EUR65 from EUR60 and kept Buy. It lifted FY26 adj. EBITDA by about 3% to EUR10,060m, near the high end of the EUR9.6-10.1bn guidance range. Its Q4 underlying EBITDA forecast of EUR1,848m is 5% above Bloomberg consensus. The target change reflects an 11x multiple on Pharma in the SoTP, up from 10x.

DB raised its GEA (G1AG.DE) target to EUR78 from EUR76 and kept Buy, citing a record order backlog, margin expansion and stronger cash generation. It lifted FY27E and FY28E revenue and EBITDA by 2% each. GEA trades at 12.7x EV/EBITDA, a 12% discount to the Stoxx 600 Industrials versus a historical 2% premium.

DB raised its Skanska (SKAb.ST) target to SEK325 from SEK300 and kept Buy. It forecasts 24% EPS growth this year and a 17% CAGR over three years, after a Q3 construction book-to-bill of 128% and a record backlog. FY27/28 EPS forecasts rose 5%, and the stock trades below 15x FY27E P/E.

DB reiterated Buy on Coca-Cola Hellenic (CCH.L) with a 5,620p target (last close 4,224p) after an 18% pullback. It estimates a CY27 P/E of 18.7x excluding Russia but including CCBA. A 24x P/E on that basis implies 5,413p, or 32% upside.

DB reiterated Buy on CTP (CTPNV.AS) with a EUR15 target. CTP proposed a roughly USD500m acquisition of a Vietnam logistics portfolio and operating platform. DB's rough calculation suggests a yield on cost below the 10%+ CTP expects, and about 150bps of additional LTV.

DB reiterated Buy on Knights Group (KGHK.L) with a 250p target (last close 162p). H2 26 organic revenue growth was 11% y/y and fee earner productivity is up 30% since FY19. DB forecasts FY27E revenue growth of about 5%.

DB kept Buy on Theon International (THEON.AS) with a EUR39 target after Q3 revenue of EUR134.1m (3% above DB) and adjusted EBIT of EUR35.1m (2% above DB, 26.2% margin). Mid-term growth guidance was raised on order momentum.

DB kept Hold on UniCredit (CRDI.MI) with a EUR78 target (last close EUR81.62). Net profit of EUR3.26bn was 14% above DB and 17% above consensus. NII rose 8% y/y and trading profits were EUR293mn against about EUR90mn expected. CET1 and interim distributions beat expectations, and 2026 and 2028 guidance improved.

DB kept Hold on Almirall (ALM.MC) with a EUR13 target. Q3 revenue was 3% below DB and 2% below consensus, with Ebglyss sales of EUR47.6m below estimates despite 56% y/y growth. Reported EBITDA beat DB by 44% and consensus by 9%. German pricing reform from January 2027 remains an uncertainty.

DB kept Hold on Kainos (KNOS.L) with a 1,260p target (last close 1,077p). H1 revenue of GBP268.8m (+37% y/y) and adjusted PBT of GBP41.7m (+30%) beat DB's GBP256.1m and GBP39.5m. The adjusted PBT margin fell to 15.5% from 16.3%, and near-term operational gearing is limited.

DB's Goodyear (GT.OQ) note keeps Hold with a USD4 target. The board named Roger Wood interim CEO five days after a Q3 print in which Americas margin fell to 3.6%. Americas segment operating income fell to $96m from $206m y/y and YTD operating cash flow is -$764m. DB thinks an operator in the chair raises the odds of footprint action.

DB kept Buy on Target Hospitality (TH.OQ) with a USD23 target (last close USD11.06). Q3 revenue was 3% and EBITDA 5% above DB, and FY26 guidance and the annualized FY27 exit run-rate targets were maintained. The actionable pipeline now exceeds 25,000 beds against 20,000 before, though the stock is under pressure from the political and regulatory backdrop around data center construction.

DB kept Buy on Garrett Motion (GTX.OQ) with a USD30 target after an NDR with the CFO and CTO. The company is shifting toward industrial technology, and the non-passenger car business is its highest-margin segment. Genset coverage has expanded from 2.5-3 MW to 6 MW.

DB's Europe airline pricing update shows transatlantic business class fares advertised in October up 15% at 30 days out, 16% at 60 days and 18% at 180 days. Intra-EU 4Q26 seat capacity is tracking +0.4% versus +3.1% three months ago. The 60-day and 180-day fares softened sequentially, which DB does not see as a concern.

DB's European airports note says Q4 seat capacity at key airports, except Madrid, is declining y/y or moderating against Q3. Consumer confidence is slipping, and DB prefers inflation-hedged exposure, naming Groupe ADP on potential regulatory clarity before 18 November.

DB's weekly IQVIA Rx trackers cover Roche, Sanofi, Novartis, Novo Nordisk, AstraZeneca, GSK, small/mid-cap pharma and vaccines, with data to 30 October 2026. Trends are mostly unchanged from prior weeks, and Rx-implied variance versus consensus is flagged by asset.

DB's Novartis (NOVN.S) note keeps Sell with a CHF115 target (last close CHF133.46). The full pelacarsen HORIZON data showed a 78% Lp(a) reduction, but MACE curves were nearly identical to placebo. DB views this as neutral and the remibrutinib MS feedback as a very minor positive.

DB's weekly flu update says US CDC data show an early flu season start. The CDC forecasts 6,900-30,100 new flu hospital admissions for the week ending 21 November 2026, 2-8x the same week last year. DB sees support for respiratory testing volumes.

earnings_insights: Hugo Boss: Q3 call said wholesale order intake for the upcoming season is below the prior year. DB cut EBIT forecasts by about 3% (FY26), 23% (FY27) and 19% (FY28). It is about 16% below consensus for FY27 and 23% below for FY28.
SOBI: Q3 was a beat and raise reported 27/10/26. The IONS Q3 update cut the FY26 Tryngolza sHTG guide to $50m from $100m, with Q3 revenue of $9m.

Bayer: DB raised FY26 adj. EBITDA by about 3% to EUR10,060m against company guidance of EUR9.6-10.1bn. DB's Q4 underlying EBITDA of EUR1,848m is 5% above Bloomberg consensus (FY consensus less 9M actuals). FY26 EPS rose about 1%.
GEA: Q3/26 reported a record order backlog, margin expansion and stronger cash generation. DB raised FY27E and FY28E revenue and EBITDA by 2%.
Skanska: Q3 results were largely in line, with EPS +35% y/y reported. Construction 12-month book-to-bill was 128%. DB forecasts 24% EPS growth this year and a 17% CAGR over three years.
Theon: Q3 revenue of EUR134.1m reported was 3% above DB. Adjusted EBIT of EUR35.1m reported was 2% above DB, a 26.2% margin against DB's 26.3% estimate. Net debt closed at EUR251m.

Almirall: Q3 group revenue was 3% below DB and 2% below consensus. Ebglyss sales were EUR47.6m reported, 15% below DB and 7% below BBG, despite 56% y/y growth. Reported EBITDA was 44% above DB and 9% above consensus. Reported net income was 82% above DB and 28% below consensus.

Kainos: H1 revenue of GBP268.8m reported (+37% y/y) against DB's GBP256.1m. Adjusted PBT of GBP41.7m (+30%) against DB's GBP39.5m. Adjusted diluted EPS rose 45% to 27.4p and interim DPS rose 6% to 10.4p.

UniCredit: Net profit of EUR3.26bn reported was 14% above DB and 17% above consensus. NII was +8% y/y and 3% above DB and consensus. Fees were +10% y/y. Trading profits were EUR293mn against about EUR90mn expected. Costs fell 1% y/y and LLPs were 18bps.
Target Hospitality: Q3 revenue beat DB by 3% and EBITDA by 5%. WHS revenue beat DB by 4%. FY26 revenue and EBITDA outlook was maintained.
Goodyear: Q3 2026 Americas margin was 3.6% reported. Americas segment operating income was $96m against $206m a year earlier. YTD operating cash flow is -$764m.
Informa: TechTarget (57% owned) delivered poor 3Q trading and cut FY guidance. TechTarget is below 3% of Informa's post-tax earnings.

trade_ideas.description: Hugo Boss downgraded to Sell, target EUR30.5 from EUR42
trade_ideas.rationale: Falling sales, distribution reset, weak wholesale order intake and EBIT forecasts well below consensus.
An 18% pullback offers an entry point, with CY27 P/E of 18.7x ex-Russia with CCBA versus 24x implied value.

trade_ideas.description: Groupe ADP preferred among European airports on potential regulatory clarity
trade_ideas.rationale: The ERA proposals provide inflation-linked tariffs and risk-sharing, and DB prefers inflation hedges when yields are high.
trade_ideas.risk: The ERA decision is due before 18 November.

risk_factors: Hugo Boss: wholesale order intake below the prior year, a distribution network still resetting and missing operating leverage.
SOBI: CEO departure at year end with no successor named, and a weaker Tryngolza sHTG launch.
CTP: higher leverage (about 150bps higher LTV) and a possible yield below target on the Vietnam acquisition.
Almirall: uncertainty around German pricing reform from January 2027.
Target Hospitality: political and regulatory backdrop around new data center construction.
European airports: falling seat capacity, slipping consumer confidence and an uncertain geopolitical and macro backdrop.
geopolitical: The European airports note describes the geopolitical and macro backdrop as uncertain despite a recent dip in oil prices.
The Target Hospitality note cites the political and regulatory backdrop around new data center construction.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 beat and raise sent the stock to new highs, and the present business is growing at strong double digits ahead of the Tryngolza sHTG launch.
tension_points.bear_case: The IONS Q3 update cut the FY26 Tryngolza guide to $50m from $100m, with only $9m in Q3 revenue. The CEO leaves at year end with no successor.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A successful Tryngolza sHTG launch ramp, which DB has flagged as the key issue.

tension_points.bull_case: An 18% pullback offers an entry point, and 24x on a post-CCBA ex-Russia business implies 5,413p, or 32% upside.
tension_points.bear_case: The business in Russia is a risk, though DB expects superior returns with or without it.
